correctness.rationale: Step 1 proves the finite conditional geometric law and the simultaneous maximum over n absolute log-size errors is o_P(n) by two geometric tail inequalities. Step 2 gives the marked Poisson extreme limit from a triangular independent rare-event array with finite-score and late-index tail truncations. Step 3 factors its marks from top score spacings and computes the Exp(1) gap by the unit-rate Poisson arrival transformation. Step 4 uses the strictly positive limiting score gap to control actual maximizers and the top-two log-population gap. Step 5 deterministically bounds the difference between that gap and negative log aggregate minority mass by 2 log n. This supplies convergence for all fixed finite thresholds and all n→∞. The exact-rational finite checks (228 passed) corroborate selected premises only; no finite experiment is treated as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: A growing-population selective sweep is naturally quantified not only by whether one family dominates but by the precise exponential rate of total surviving competitor mass, and how that rate relates to the dominant founder’s age. The new joint nondegenerate independent exponential law answers both questions exactly on the natural n/log n and n scales, exposing a statistic not given by qualitative dominance or leader-process convergence alone. This is a motivated structural limiting invariant. Constraints include uniform fitness, geometric independent offspring and no extinction; no general universality or finite-n error bounds are claimed.
